headline: Committee defers Bill 93-2024 on emergency donations without taking a vote

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: The bill would let the County accept emergency donations without prior Council approval, with spending limited to emergency management and approved in writing by the mayor. The chair deferred it; the next committee meeting is October 20th.
meeting.recap: The committee took up Bill 93-2024, Chair Lee's bill about money donated during an emergency.[[0:08:55]] The bill would let the County accept these donations without first getting Council approval.[[0:09:19]] The money could be used only for emergency management work.[[0:09:32]] The mayor would approve spending in writing and report to the Council every quarter.[[0:09:39]] One testifier, James Langford, supported the bill's oversight.[[0:22:39]] An administration speaker said County wildfire donations were used for the Lahaina Homecoming.[[0:44:34]] A member suggested forming a TIG, a group of Council members, to work on these ideas.[[0:51:20]] The next committee meeting is October 20th.[[0:56:01]] The committee chair deferred the bill, so no vote was taken.[[1:00:10]]

moments.q: "Over $140 million is a lot of money, and we need to have some kind of oversight"
"This is a much better written bill than the conversation kind of reflects"
